generated.title: SIX SEVEN vs FOUR TWO: The Earthquake Difference #shorts
generated.description:
SIX SEVEN vs FOUR TWO: which earthquake releases more energy?

A magnitude 6.7 earthquake releases about 5,600 times the seismic energy of a magnitude 4.2 earthquake. They are only two and a half magnitude units apart. According to the USGS, each whole magnitude step is about 32 times more energy (10^1.5), and 10^(1.5 x 2.5) is about 5,600. The ratio is approximate; other energy formulas give a somewhat smaller number.

The SIX SEVEN opening is wordplay on magnitude numbers, not a real event. The dot grid is an illustration of the ratio, not data or footage.

Part of the Earthquake Science Explained series. Subscribe to Next Huge Quake for more earthquake science.
